_how_it_is_used: server_scripts/grindless/uxv/vela_pasta.js makes one recipe per entry, id grindless:<name> (GTM prefixes the type), with its programmed circuit (circuit 0 = none, only where a type lists 'noCircuit'); 'site' true locks the recipe to grindless:vela_pulsar_orbit, a string names another site; 'kept' are not consumed; 'wear' is a kept input that a chance consumes (per ten thousand). pasta_extraction, pasta_sorting, pasta_drawing and pasta_lamination are package UXV-B4's machine types, polar_cap_tapping is its generator (eut is what it makes); neutronium_caging is UIV's type (a companion row with its slots in 'maxIO'). Package UXV-B4, docs/eras/uxv.md machines 16-20 and process lines 32, 33. Rows whose _why starts with OpV-A0 are the chain matter modes at grindless:sgr1806_orbit (docs/eras/opv.md process lines 1 and 2): circuits 3-5, the cage part consumed.

recipes._why: machine 16 c1: the funnel catches what the glitch crust sheds; the timing record (kept) points the receiver and one pellet in ten is spent as bait
recipes.name: pasta_extraction

recipes._why: OpV-A0 line 1, c3 at SGR 1806-20: the bulge chart (kept) points the funnel at the Fe-56 chain crust; one pellet in ten is spent as bait (opv.md rate: 1 slab per 600 t)
recipes.name: chain_crust

recipes._why: OpV-A0, c4 at SGR 1806-20: the Ni-62/64 chain layer, F1's ni_chain_slab (opv.md rate: 1 slab per 1,200 t; caged by sorting c4, thawed by OpV-B2)
recipes.name: ni_chain

recipes._why: OpV-A0 line 2, c5 at SGR 1806-20: the deeper outer crust, where the chains condense into a lattice (Medin & Lai 2006; opv.md rate: 1 slab per 600 t)
recipes.name: chain_lattice

recipes._why: machine 17 c1: a cage part (kept) holds the raw pasta while the density arc sorts it into spaghetti, lasagna, gnocchi and an anti-phase residue
recipes.name: phase_sorting

recipes._why: machine 17 c2: sixteen residues sealed in a cage part (consumed) become one core sample, the residue's only use
recipes.name: core_sample

recipes._why: OpV-A0 line 1, c3 at SGR 1806-20: a crust slab closed in a cage part (consumed: the cage leaves with the phase and is spent when the draw bench opens it); the iron that was never chained falls out as dust
recipes.name: chain_caging

recipes._why: OpV-A0, c4 at SGR 1806-20: a Ni chain slab closed in a cage part (consumed) for the trip home; OpV-B2's electron beam c23 thaws it
recipes.name: ni_chain_caging

recipes._why: OpV-A0 line 2, c5 at SGR 1806-20: a lattice slab closed in a cage part (consumed: spent when the laminator presses it); the unchained iron falls out as dust
recipes.name: lattice_caging

recipes._why: machine 18 c1: the spaghetti phase is drawn through an aerogel die into eight strands of pasta wire; a cage part (kept) holds the draw
recipes.name: strand_drawing

recipes._why: OpV-A0 line 1, c3 at SGR 1806-20: the caged chain phase is drawn out of its cage (spent) into four chain strand ingots
recipes.name: chain_strand_drawing

recipes._why: OpV-A0 line 1, c4 at SGR 1806-20: a chain strand ingot is drawn into two single wires (GTM's own wire ratio is cut by OpV-F2: the strand only draws here)
recipes.name: chain_wire_drawing

recipes._why: machine 19 c1: the lasagna phase is pressed on a rhea billet into four plates; a cage part (kept) holds the press
recipes.name: plate_pressing

recipes._why: machine 19 c2: a plate carries two strands of pasta wire as the lasagna electrode (UXV-B4's own fuel; UIV's polar_cap_electrode is a different item and is not spent by the tap)
recipes.name: lasagna_electrode

recipes._why: OpV-A0 line 2, c3 at SGR 1806-20: the caged lattice is pressed out of its cage (spent) into four chain laminae
recipes.name: chain_lamina

recipes._why: OpV-A0 line 2, c4 at SGR 1806-20: two chain laminae bonded on a lasagna plate into F1's chain lamina stack (the hull's and every OpV component's part)
recipes.name: chain_lamina_stack

recipes._why: OpV-A0 for line 6, c5 at SGR 1806-20: four PBO fibres woven around two chain strand wires; OpV-A1's electron beam welds the weave into the mesh belt
recipes.name: chain_mesh_weave

recipes._why: machine 20 c1: one lasagna electrode taps the pulsar's polar cap for 720 t at 536,870,912 EU/t (386,547,056,640 EU) and is spent; the chain that makes it costs about 1.95e11 EU, so the tap returns about 1.99x (power generous, never free)
recipes.name: polar_cap_tap

recipes._why: machine 16's cage part: UIV's cage machine closes a pellet in an mh winding (no circuit: its circuits 1 and 2 are taken)
recipes.name: cage_part_pressing
